newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha ends firmer as Skikda fears downplayed.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha ends firmer as Skikda fears downplayed.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices ended slightly higher on Monday as traders and brokers said any negative impact from Skikda's loading changes had only a short-term influence over prices.

Sonatrach was still not available for comment but sources said the Algerian state oil company was suspending double-stem loadings of naphtha for a limited time out of one of the three jetties at Skikda.
This jetty allows the largest vessels to berth but one of the other two remaining jetties will allow double-stem loadings with length restrictions, sources said.

May swaps ended about $2 higher at $179.50/$180.50 with June $2 higher. NWE cargoes were assessed near $180 cif, where pipeline spec material was offered; a Dow spec cargo was rumoured to be offered at $179 with no bids.
"Skikda had an impact last week but not this week," said one source. "People feared that cargoes would be sold into Europe (instead of Asia) and now people think they will still go east."
He added that naphtha prices were likely to drift sideways for the next few days with traders not wanting a big price move either due to cargo positioning.
